Q: What characterizes the Advanced Technology eXtended (ATX) motherboard form factor versus Information Technology eXtended (ITX)?
Option1: ATX is generally larger with more expansion slots and headers
Option2: ATX is smaller with fewer slots
Option4: ITX always has multiple CPU sockets

Q: What distinguishes Information Technology eXtended (ITX) boards?
Option2: Small-form-factor boards used in compact systems with limited slots

Q: What is Peripheral Component Interconnect (PCI) on a motherboard?
Option2: A high-speed serial lane architecture

Q: What is Peripheral Component Interconnect Express (PCIe)?
Option1: A serial expansion bus that uses lanes (x1, x4, x8, x16) for add-in cards such as graphics
Option2: A parallel ribbon bus

Q: What are 'power connectors' in this context?
Option2: Connectors supplying power from the power supply (for example, 24-pin main and 4/8-pin CPU) and SATA power for drives

Q: What is Serial ATA (SATA) on a motherboard?
Option2: A data interface for drives; distinct from the SATA power connector

Q: What is eSATA compared with SATA?
Option2: An externalized SATA interface for external drives and docks

Q: What are 'headers' on a motherboard?
Option2: Pin blocks for front-panel connections, USB, audio, and other internal cabling

Q: What is meant by CPU sockets under motherboard compatibility?
Option2: Specific mechanical and electrical interfaces for processors that are vendor and generation specific

Q: Which statement about Advanced Micro Devices and Intel sockets is correct?
Option2: Each vendor uses different socket families; compatibility depends on platform and generation
Option3: All CPUs fit any ITX board

Q: What does 'server' or 'multisocket' motherboard indicate?
Option1: Boards that support more than one processor package for higher core counts and memory capacity
Option2: Boards that only fit in laptops
Option3: Boards that cannot use ECC memory

Q: What is the purpose of Basic Input/Output System (BIOS) or Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) boot options?
Option1: Select startup devices and order (for example, solid-state drive, optical, network)
Option2: Set screen brightness

Q: What do 'USB permissions' in firmware typically control?
Option2: Allowing or blocking booting from and access to Universal Serial Bus devices

Q: What is Trusted Platform Module (TPM) in firmware settings?
Option2: A hardware security chip providing cryptographic functions such as measured boot and disk encryption key storage

Q: What does 'fan considerations' in firmware usually configure?
Option2: Fan curves or profiles for temperature-based cooling control

Q: What is Secure Boot?
Option1: A feature that allows any unsigned bootloader
Option2: A firmware feature that checks bootloaders against trusted certificates to prevent unauthorized code at startup

Q: What does a 'boot password' (setup or power-on) do?
Option2: Restricts access to firmware settings or booting without a password

Q: What is a Hardware Security Module (HSM)?
Option2: A dedicated device that safeguards and manages cryptographic keys; can integrate with servers for high-assurance operations

Q: What is x64/x86 in CPU architecture terms?
Option2: Instruction set families; x86 is 32-bit compatibility, x64 extends to 64-bit processing

Q: What is Advanced RISC Machine (ARM) in this context?
Option2: A Reduced Instruction Set architecture common in mobile and some servers emphasizing efficiency

Q: What is the difference between single-core and multicore CPUs?
Option1: Single-core has one processing core; multicore integrates multiple cores within a single package to execute more threads in parallel
Option2: Single-core is always faster

Q: What is simultaneous multithreading (often called multithreading) on a CPU?
Option2: A technology that lets one physical core schedule multiple hardware threads to improve utilization

Q: What does 'virtualization support' in a CPU/firmware enable?
Option2: Hardware acceleration for running virtual machines (for example, Intel VT-x or AMD-V)

Q: What distinguishes desktop and mobile variants of a platform?
Option2: Mobile parts are designed for lower power and thermal envelopes; desktop parts target higher performance and more slots
Option3: Mobile always has more PCIe slots

Q: What is a sound card as an expansion card?
Option1: A card providing additional or higher-quality audio inputs/outputs
Option2: A storage controller only

Q: What is a video card (graphics card)?
Option1: An add-in card providing graphics processing and display outputs via PCI Express x16
Option2: A sound interface

Q: What is a capture card?
Option1: An add-in that ingests video/audio signals for recording or streaming
Option2: A storage drive

Q: What is a network interface card (NIC)?
Option1: A card that provides Ethernet or other network connectivity
Option2: A speaker amplifier

Q: What is the role of fans in cooling?
Option2: Move air to remove heat from components and heat sinks

Q: What is a heat sink?
Option2: A thermal mass with fins that draws heat from a component, often with a fan

Q: What do thermal paste or thermal pads do?
Option2: Fill microscopic gaps to conduct heat between a component and a heat sink

Q: What characterizes liquid cooling?
Option1: Uses a pumped coolant and radiator to transfer heat away from components
Option2: Cools using only passive airflow
Option4: Replaces the need for a heat sink

Q: A new graphics card is not detected after installation. Which motherboard slot should it use for best performance?
Option2: PCI Express x16

Q: A system fails to boot from the new solid-state drive. First best step in firmware?
Option2: Change the boot order to place the solid-state drive first or enable the controller

Q: Users cannot boot from Universal Serial Bus media despite a valid installer. Likely firmware control to review?
Option1: USB permissions and boot device control
Option2: Fan curve profile

Q: You need to deploy full-disk encryption with keys bound to hardware. Which components work together?
Option2: Trusted Platform Module with operating system encryption

Q: A virtualization lab will run multiple virtual machines. Which settings must be enabled?
Option2: CPU virtualization extensions in firmware and adequate multicore processors

Q: A high-density server requires two physical processors. Which motherboard feature is required?
Option2: Multisocket support

Q: How does Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) compare to legacy BIOS?
Option2: UEFI replaces legacy BIOS with a modern firmware interface (GPT support, Secure Boot, rich boot options)

Q: What are motherboard 'front-panel headers' used for?
Option2: Wiring the case switches/LEDs (power switch, reset, HDD LED, power LED) and sometimes speaker

Q: When applying a heat sink, what does thermal paste/Pad actually do?
Option2: Fills microscopic gaps to improve heat transfer between CPU and heat sink
